front: How many UUIDv4s for a 50% chance of one collision?
back: About √(2 · ln 2 · 2^122) ≈ 2.7 × 10^18, about 86 years at a billion a second.

front: Why do random UUID keys slow B-tree inserts at scale?
back: Each insert hits a random leaf page: cold reads from disk once the index outgrows memory, plus page splits and half-empty pages.
A native 16-byte type (uuid, BINARY(16)), never a 36-character string.

front: Four problems with auto-increment at scale?
back: Breaks under sharding, ID only exists after insert, leaks volume, has gaps by design.
They are non-transactional: a rolled-back insert still consumes its number.
Two MySQL servers bumping an auto-increment, one issuing odd and one even IDs; clients alternate.
Each app server takes a block of IDs (say 1,000) and hands them out from memory. Fewer round trips; gaps on restart.
1 sign bit, 41 bits ms since custom epoch, 10 bits machine ID, 12 bits sequence.
4,096 IDs per ms per machine (about 4.1 million/s), 1,024 machines, 2^41 ms ≈ 69.7 years.
41 bits of ms last about 69.7 years; counting from 1970 would waste decades already spent.

front: Clock goes backwards under Snowflake: defences?
back: Track last timestamp; wait for small jumps, refuse and alert on big ones, or use max(now, last). Configure NTP to slew, not step.

front: How do containers get unique machine IDs?
back: Claim one through a lease (etcd, ZooKeeper, a DB row); stop generating if the lease is lost.
